gaps.sentence: He ___ some ridiculous excuse about his car breaking down.
gaps.explanation: make an excuse is the fixed collocation; 'tell an excuse' is not used.

gaps.sentence: I ___ a strange dream last night.
gaps.explanation: have a dream is the English collocation; 'see a dream' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: She ___ attention to every detail of the contract.
I was nearly late, but I managed to ___ the last bus.
gaps.hint: to get on a bus or train in time
gaps.explanation: catch a bus/train means to arrive in time to board it; the words 'managed to' and 'nearly late' show success.

gaps.sentence: We ___ a visit to the museum while we were in Vienna.
gaps.explanation: pay a visit to somebody/something means to go and see them briefly.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to the conclusion that the project was not viable.
gaps.explanation: come to the conclusion that ... is the fixed phrase; 'reach' and 'arrive' do not take 'to'.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ attention when the teacher is speaking.
gaps.explanation: pay attention is the fixed collocation for listening or concentrating carefully.

gaps.sentence: She ___ a quick shower before leaving the gym.
gaps.explanation: have a shower is the standard British English collocation; 'made a shower' is wrong.
